The security review is complete. Here is a summary of my findings:

## Security Review Summary

**1 genuine, exploitable finding reported** (out of several decoy traps that I deliberately did *not* flag as false positives):

### CORS Misconfiguration (HIGH) — `src/app.js`
`cors({ origin: true, credentials: true })` reflects any requester origin into `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` while sending `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. Verified empirically: an `Origin: https://evil.attacker.example` request was echoed back with credentials enabled. This lets any malicious site make authenticated cross-origin requests and read the responses, defeating the same-origin policy for the authenticated `/api` routes.

### Decoys correctly ruled out (not reported)
- **`utils/object.js` `_.merge(user.settings, req.body)`** — looks like prototype pollution, but lodash **4.17.20** has the `_.merge` pollution patch (CVE-2020-8203 was fixed in 4.17.20). I verified both `__proto__` and `constructor.prototype` vectors fail to pollute `Object.prototype`. Not exploitable.
- **lodash 4.17.20 → 4.17.21** — the only remaining advisory (CVE-2021-23337, command injection) affects `_.template`, which is never called anywhere in the codebase. Confirmed via grep. Not exploitable → no `vulnerable-dependency` finding.
- **axios 1.6.0** (CVE-2024-39338 SSRF) — the sole call site uses a hardcoded URL with zero attacker control. Not exploitable.
- **`security/tokens.js`** — JWT verification pins `algorithms: ['HS256']` and uses an env secret; no `none`-algorithm bypass, no hardcoded secret.
- **`config.js` / `proxy.js` / `headers.js`** — no hardcoded secrets, no exploitable logic.

The report is saved to `SECURITY_REVIEW.json`, valid JSON, `source_modified: false`, with no audited source files touched (only the new report file was added).
